results.title: Spectacled cobras in India genetically same despite visible differences
results.description: Kolkata, Aug 25 (IANS) The Evolutionary Venomics Lab (EVL) has carried out vital research on the spectacled cobra (Naja naja), one of the most venomous snakes found in nearly all parts of the country. This snake contributes to nearly 58,000 snakebite deaths in India annually. Hence, the research is crucial in developing more efficient anti-venoms to save lives. The research has also all but dispelled the theory that spectacled cobras migrated from Asia to Africa. In fact, it is the other way around. N. naja moved to Asia from Africa during the Miocene (23 to 5.3 million years ago). It moved through the Middle East. These reptiles then moved from India to Sri Lanka millions of years ago. "The spectacled cobra is among the most iconic and clinically significant species, recognised as one of India’s ‘big four’ snakes responsible for a large number of snakebite-related fatalities. As a generalist with a near-countrywide distribution, N. naja exhibits considerable geographic variation in morphology, behaviour, and venom composition. Yet, its evolutionary history, phylogenetic diversity, and biogeographical origins remain poorly understood," a research paper published by the lab says. Researchers sequenced nuclear and mitochondrial markers from nearly 100 snakes across the major biogeographical regions of the Indian subcontinent to fill this knowledge gap. "Our results support an African origin for the genus Naja and support a Miocene dispersal of N. naja into South Asia. Unlike many widely distributed snakes, N. naja does not exhibit any evidence of phylogeographic subdivision within India, indicating that it is a largely panmictic mainland species," the researchers have said. Kartik Sunagar, an associate professor at EVL who has been involved in this research, explains what this means. "This is not just a matter of naming snakes. When a species is spread across a vast area, rivers, mountains, deserts, climate, or sea-level changes can separate populations. Over thousands or millions of years, these isolated populations may evolve independently. Eventually, what we once called one species may turn out to be several," he writes. After the research, "Across mainland India, the spectacled cobra appears to be largely one connected genetic population. Despite all the visible variation in colour, marking, ecology, and venom, the genetic data did not support the presence of multiple deeply separated species," he says. So, why is this important? "If different populations have different venoms, evolutionary histories, or levels of relatedness, the knowledge can influence how we think of anti-venom, conservation and snakebite biology," Sunagar explains on his website. However, the Sri Lankan N. naja, which the researcher believes moved to the island from India when sea levels were low, is genetically distinct. Such research is extremely important for developing anti-venoms. In 2024, the EVL developed a synthetic anti-venom. The ultimate aim is to bring down the number of anti-venoms that need to be stocked to treat snakebites. --IANS jg/dan

results.title: ‘Unemployed Rights Elgar’: NCP (SP) announces Tricolour motorcycle rally
results.description: Mumbai, Aug 25 (IANS) Taking an aggressive stance on the issue of rising unemployment in Maharashtra, the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) on Tuesday announced a state-wide tricolour motorcycle rally titled ‘Berozgar Hakk Elgar’ (Unemployed Rights Elgar) on August 27. The rally will take place across all districts and administrative divisions in the state. Through this protest, the party aims to highlight several key demands, including ensuring jobs for locals in Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) zones, filling vacant government posts immediately, preventing exam paper leaks, and completing police recruitment drives on time. The motorcycle rallies will launch from key locations in each district and division and end at the respective District Collectorates. Regional leadership for the rallies has already been assigned. In Mumbai, National Working President and MP Supriya Sule, along with State President Shashikant Shinde, will lead the protest. In Vidarbha (Nagpur), former minister Anil Deshmukh will lead; in Marathwada (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), former minister Rajesh Tope; in North Maharashtra (Nashik), MLAs Rohit Pawar and Sunil Bhusara; in Western Maharashtra, Jayant Patil and Harshvardhan Patil; and in Konkan Division (Thane), MLA Jitendra Awhad. NCP (SP) has demanded regular and timely recruitment for vacant positions across all government departments, re-establishment of employment exchange centres in every Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation zone specifically for residents, creation of an action plan to guarantee jobs for locals based on their qualifications, stringent action against those involved in exam paper leaks and recruitment malpractices, immediate clearing of the recruitment backlog in reserved categories, and prioritising regular government employment for qualified youth over contractual hiring. It has also demanded urgent recruitment to fill vacant positions in the police force, ensuring candidates do not cross the age eligibility limit due to procedural delays, and the announcement of concrete, district-wise job-creation programmes. Meanwhile, NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar visited the ongoing agitation of tribal students in Manjari (Pune) and spoke with them. "Today, in the meeting of MLAs convened by the Minister, it came to light that the Minister of the Tribal Department himself was speaking negatively about the students’ demands, which is extremely unfortunate. However, due to pressure from the students, it has been learned that all MLAs from the tribal community will meet the Chief Minister tonight,” he said. He added that concrete decisions must be made on the students’ demands; otherwise, this agitation will intensify further, and if justice is not served, the students themselves will demand the resignation of the ministers from this department; they should consider this as well. “But under no circumstances should there be a withdrawal from the agitation until the demands are accepted; we are all together with them; this assurance was given to these students,” he said. --IANS sj/dan
